questions.prompt: Why does a child agent reject every ask instead of showing it to a person?
options: Asks from a child are always unsafe
The person watches the parent's chat, so a child's question would wait with nobody to answer
The child has no approval service at all
The parent answers every ask for the child
questions.explanation: Nobody watches the child's session. The policy never rejects the ask at once, and the child reports the limit in its reply.

questions.prompt: The parent switches to read-only mode one second after it delegates. Which mode does the child have?
options: Read-only, because the child follows the parent live
The mode the parent had at delegation, because it was captured before any await
Full access, because a child has no sandbox
No mode until the child asks for one
questions.explanation: The tool reads the parent's mode before its first await and logs it in the child's record. A later parent change belongs to the parent only.

questions.prompt: Why does setup append the policy as events in the child's record?
options: So the child's record alone shows what it could do, even after a resume
So the parent's model can read the policy
Because tools can only be restricted through events
So the person can change the policy from the child's chat
questions.explanation: The events make the policy part of the child's record. A resumed child rebuilds the same limits from its own file.
